mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-46.3 to -43.0), indicating a steady recovery trend in discretionary mobility that should persist and continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior three-week improving streak.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has risen sharply (-72.3 to -65.4 over four weeks), suggesting increased outdoor and local-area activity that spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within one to two weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC upward.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved by nearly 7 points over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of a sustained week-on-week increase in PARKS of more than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility rebounds by more than 5 points within a single week from its current depressed level (-36.4), this signals a rapid loosening of restrictions that would also drive a commensurate rise in RETAIL_REC within the following week as commuting-adjacent shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has moved narrowly between -38.6 and -36.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in TRANSIT usage and decrease in RESIDENTIAL time indicates compounding relaxation of stay-at-home behavior, where the joint effect of more transit trips and less home-dwelling produces a larger boost to RETAIL_REC than either factor alone, especially given TRANSIT's 4.5-point gain and RESIDENTIAL's stabilization near 12.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously falls or plateaus week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -46.4 to -41.9 while RESIDENTIAL plateaued near 11.7-13.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over four weeks despite concurrent TRANSIT increases and RESIDENTIAL stabilization or decline.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above 15 points week-on-week, this signals a renewed policy tightening or voluntary sheltering response that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks as households reduce non-essential outings.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained between 11.7 and 13.3 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL crosses above 15 but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As mid-September progresses toward autumn, PARKS mobility gains observed to date are expected to reverse due to seasonal cooling and shorter daylight hours, reducing outdoor substitution effects and causing RETAIL_REC growth to plateau or reverse over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-09-15, entering autumn season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks despite seasonal decline expectations and no reversal in PARKS trend.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in RETAIL_REC's week-on-week improvement rate (from +1.3 to +0.1 to +2.1 points) suggests the recovery is losing momentum and approaching a plateau, implying the next four weeks will show flat-to-slightly-negative movement rather than continued strong gains.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week RETAIL_REC improvement falls below 1.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly deltas were +1.3, -0.1, +2.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at an accelerating or stable pace over the next four weeks despite the observed deceleration pattern.
